key_insight: The study introduces UPEBNL, a scalable causal Bayesian network framework that makes large-scale EHR-based cancer prescreening more interpretable and computationally practical.
clinical_relevance: By revealing evidence paths and directional dependencies, the model could help support more transparent cancer risk stratification for esophageal and colorectal prescreening.
method: Adaptive data slicing for parallel causal Bayesian network learning
Quality-aware structure aggregation to stabilize learned dependencies
Global DAG construction to combine submodels into one interpretable network
evidence_signal: In simulations, UPEBNL improved structural recovery by nearly 40% and sped up learning by up to 221.28-fold; in EHR prescreening, it reached AUCs of 0.8171 for esophageal cancer and 0.784 for colorectal cancer.
watch_item: The approach still depends on observational EHR data, so learned causal directions may reflect data quality and confounding rather than confirmed biological causality.
paper_title: Scalable Causal-Interpretable Machine Learning for Cancer Prescreening Using Electronic Health Records
